title: Move NVIDIA PiD out of the model picker into the image upscale dropdown, as four plugins
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-553 - Upscalers leave the model picker, as plugins (project-refresh consolidation sweep 2026-08-13). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-553/plan.md.

Fabio, 2026-08-09: 'PiD has four different models instead of being a separate model, which at the moment doesn't make much sense because it's a model that just upscales and doesn't generate anything. PiD will also come in the upscale dropdown for images in the History workspace. I honestly think it's a much better home for these types of models, and it will make our upscale section much more valuable.'

Depends on the plugin-contributes-a-dropdown-entry mechanism built in MPI-506 - build it there, reuse it here unchanged. MPI-506 is additive and can land alone; this one is a migration that touches a shipped model, a shipped Flow and the release gate, so land 506 first.

THE SPLIT PAYS OFF: all four PiD paths are 1024->4096 4-step bf16, 2.54GB each, plus a per-path VAE (0.17-0.34GB) and ONE shared mandatory gemma text encoder at 5.23GB. Today it is all-or-nothing at 16.48GB to use any single path. As four plugins, the SDXL path alone costs ~8.1GB and each extra path ~2.8GB, with pluginRequiredDepIds() keeping the shared encoder alive while any PiD plugin remains installed.

THE DROPDOWN IS THE EASY PART. Three real problems, detailed in brief.md: (a) the pid op declares components ['pidVariant','pidResolution','denoise'] plus an optional prompt, all of which live in the PromptBox - MpiToolOptionsUpscale has none of them. pidVariant dies with the split (the plugin IS the variant) but prompt/denoise/resolution need a decision: drop them, or grow the tool panel. That decision sets the card's size. (b) PiD is fixed 4x, so the tool's x1.5/x2/x3/x4 factor radio has no meaning and must be hidden or reinterpreted, not silently ignored. (c) flowsRegistry.js:107 has flowSdxl4k declaring requiredModels ['sdxl-nsfw','nvidia-pid'] and its comment says it DELIBERATELY exercises the multi-model install path, so deleting the ModelDef breaks the Flow and removes that coverage - preferred fix is to keep the ModelDef and hide it from the picker.

HARD RULE FOR THE REMOVAL HALF: do NOT delete the pid-* / vae-* / pid-gemma dep entries. The orphan sweep reads DEPS, so a deleted entry strands those weights on existing users' disks forever (MPI-470 and MPI-466 both kept theirs). Follow docs/playbooks/add-model/README.md section 'Removing or re-tiering a model'. Also sweep dev_configs/smoke-evidence.json, which names nvidia-pid twice and gates npm run release:check.

DECIDED 2026-08-09, two of the three problems closed. (a) Fabio: 'PiD has Denoise and Prompt Box Input, so we can just add a Text Input in the toolbar and the Denoise when PiD is selected.' Grow the panel, conditionally - pidVariant disappears (the plugin IS the variant), pidResolution is absorbed by the factor radio, and denoise + an optional text input appear only when a PiD entry is selected, defaulting to denoise 0.0 and an empty prompt. Build it as MPI-506's declared per-entry control list, not an if(isPid) branch: SeedVR2 is the opposite extreme and declares NO extra controls (verified - it takes no prompt and has no denoise), so both cases must work on day one. (b) Fabio: 'I can add the missing resolutions so that it matches what we have: 1.5, 2K, 3K, 4K' - the pidResolution switch grows until all four radio positions resolve, and the radio stays as-is. Still to settle: the radio's labels are multipliers today but PiD's are absolute targets, so either the labels go absolute everywhere or the radio relabels per entry. Only 3c (the flowSdxl4k dependency) remains open.

TWO MORE ANSWERS, 2026-08-09. (1) PiD IS IMAGE-ONLY (Fabio: 'PiD is an image upscaler, so it cannot land on the video workspace') - its entries are scoped to imageUpscale and must never reach the video dropdown. That makes MPI-506's entry declaration need a TOOL SCOPE field: SeedVR2 declares both tools, PiD declares image only. (2) FABIO ASKED IF HE NEEDS FOUR WORKFLOWS - NO, ONE, with three injected literals. Checked nvidia_pid.json node by node: the four branches are structurally identical and differ only in UNETLoader.unet_name, VAELoader.vae_name and PiDConditioning.latent_format. Everything else is shared or duplicated verbatim - all four BasicScheduler are simple/4/1, all four SamplerCustom are add_noise true/cfg 1 pointing at the same KSamplerSelect, negative, latent and seed, all four VAEEncode read the same pixels, and the gemma CLIPLoader plus the pixel_space VAELoader are already single. latent_format is a COMBO with a fixed option list so it is always valid. Collapsing drops 43 nodes to ~25 and deletes the Input_Type switch.

AND THE FOUR-BRANCH SHAPE ACTIVELY BREAKS UNDER PLUGINS, which is what forces the change rather than merely recommending it. unet_name is a COMBO from the diffusion_models folder listing; ComfyUI's validate_prompt walks every node reachable from the outputs and rejects an unknown combo value with value_not_in_list, and that check runs BEFORE execution so lazy pruning never applies. All four UNETLoaders feed the switch, so all four are reachable. It only works today because installing nvidia-pid installs all four weights; a user with just the SDXL plugin would have three names that are not on disk and the prompt would be rejected. One injected loader fixes it by construction. (klein-4b's one-master-template pattern does not hit this - it has a single checkpoint.) While the graph is open: Input_Resolution has only three entries today (1024, 2048, passthrough), so 3072 and 4096 go there and the passthrough needs a decision.

PID'S RESOLUTION PROBLEM IS A TRAINING-REGIME PROBLEM, NOT A UI ONE - Fabio to bench (2026-08-09: 'Unless I change how PiD works and adopt the same technique, I'm not sure if that's gonna work. I'll need to test it'). Every PiD checkpoint is pid_*_1024_to_4096_4step_bf16, and the graph enforces exactly that: MpiScaledDimensions normalises the input to 1024 (side use_max) through an MpiCrop at divisible_by 16, and a second MpiScaledDimensions at 4096 sizes the EmptyChromaRadianceLatentImage. PiD is a FIXED 4x TRAINED AT ONE INPUT SIZE, which is why the multiplier that works for SeedVR2 does not transfer.

TWO TECHNIQUES, THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY. A - native then downscale: always run 1024->4096 as trained and resize the OUTPUT to the target. Cannot go off-regime so correctness needs no testing, but 1K and 2K then cost the same time and VRAM as 4K on the slowest tool in the app. B - scale the input and keep 4x: feed 512 for 2K, 256 for 1K. Stays at the trained ratio but changes the absolute input resolution, and PixelDiT patching may be resolution-sensitive. B is the one to test, and if it holds it is strictly better than A. Cheap decider: run B at 512->2048 against A at 1024->4096-downscaled-to-2048 on the same source and compare.

Also noted from the live graph: PiD's sampler regime is its own - KSamplerSelect is 'lcm' at 4 steps, against SeedVR2's plain KSampler euler at 1 step. Nothing transfers between the two graphs except the tool that launches them.

DECIDED 2026-08-09, FOUR SEPARATE PID WORKFLOWS. Fabio: 'I will export 4 different workflows for PiD. All of them will have this input resolution setting.' That fully solves the validation trap - each file names only its own weight, so a user holding one plugin never has an unresolvable unet_name. Cost to accept knowingly: any shared fix lands four times, and the plugin entry must carry WHICH WORKFLOW FILE it runs instead of the op mapping to one file the way workflows:{pid:'nvidia_pid.json'} does today. Benefit beyond the fix: the four VAE-locked paths stay independently tunable.

RESOLUTION RESOLVED AS TECHNIQUE A, ALREADY BUILT. Observed in the live graph: three MpiScaledDimensions at 1024/2048/3072 all take their image input from VAEDecode, and Input_Resolution selects between them with any_4 passing the raw 4096 through (note reads 1=1k, 2=2k, 3=3k, 4=4k). PiD always generates at its trained 1024->4096 and the target is a downscale of the finished image, so correctness needs no bench. THE ONE THING TO SURFACE IN THE UI: 1K is not faster than 4K - every target costs a full 4096 generation on the slowest tool in the app. Technique B (scale the input, keep 4x) stays the upgrade path if that becomes a complaint.

DO NOT COPY FOUR-FILES TO SEEDVR2. PiD's paths differ in three literals and are VAE-locked to different architectures; SeedVR2's three variants differ in exactly ONE literal (unet_name) and share one VAE, which is why its 3B and 7B image templates are node-for-node identical. SeedVR2 wants TWO files, one per tool, with unet_name injected from the selected plugin - safe for the same reason four PiD files are safe. Net across both cards: 4 PiD files + 2 SeedVR2 files = 6 workflows. Only 3c (the flowSdxl4k dependency) is still open.
